title: Delivery plan and handoff brief drafted from deal records and call transcripts
problem: Context is lost between the deal team and the delivery team, and each new team member is briefed by hand.
approach: An agent drafts delivery plans and architecture documents from the statement of work, deal record and transcripts; the architect signs off.
Spaulding Ridge's executive chair says its Moonnox agent cut drafting a solution architecture document from about 80 hours to under 20 (self-reported).
Certinia's results panel lists 60% faster client onboarding without naming the agent or customer (vendor-published).
Engagement and delivery leads approve the handoff pack against the signed statement of work before kickoff.

title: Meeting capture turned into summaries, action items and backlogs, with consent controls
problem: Consultants spend hours writing call notes, requirements and technical plans, and onboarding teams take detailed notes and follow up by hand.
approach: AI turns meeting transcripts into summaries, decisions, action items, requirements and backlogs, and a person checks them before they circulate.
Diabsolut cut documentation time by 70% with agents in Slack (vendor-published); EarthWise Pet's in-house team uses Rocketlane call summaries.
In a study of 12 Finnish IT project-management consultants, two used meeting transcription; effects are interviewee-reported, not measurements (independent).
The meeting organiser confirms consent before recording; the owner checks the summary and action list before they go to the client.

title: Agent-drafted status reports and steering-committee packs from live project data
problem: Project managers assemble status packs by hand from budgets, task lists, emails and notes; in Wellingtone's report, 72% spend half a day or more collating reports monthly.
approach: A model grounded in the engagement's own data drafts the status report or steering pack; the project manager edits and sends it.
Nextview's Project Assistant in Slack assembles steering-committee reports; Nextview says they used to take hours and now generate with a click (vendor-published).
PwC US markets Intelligent Status Insights; its page projects about 40% lower administrative project overhead (vendor-published), naming no client.
The project manager reviews each draft before it reaches the steering committee or client.

title: Ask for project status, budget use and anomalies in plain language
problem: At zeb, project managers had to navigate the right paths and apps in SAP to find project information, often in a different context from their question.
approach: zeb and NTT DATA built SAP agents that answer plain-language questions on owners, timelines and status, forecast budget use and flag anomalies.
zeb's head of SAP solutions says the implementation took only a few weeks (vendor-published); no figures published.
The project manager reads the answer and decides; the case study does not describe formal review steps.

title: Agents flag slipping milestones, missing time entries and project health risks
problem: Slippage and overdue milestones surface late, and project managers chase status, missing time entries and overdue tasks by hand.
approach: Agents scan project records on a schedule, score health and route alerts to the project manager or PMO leader.
Siemens Digital Industries' SVP says Certinia's Project Agent, built on Salesforce, is making early discrepancy identification a reality across thousands of projects.
Deltek says firms on its platform see a 16% increase in on-time project delivery (vendor-published); method not stated.
The project manager acts on each flag; the agent identifies anomalies but does not change records.

title: Scope-drift detection against agreed scope, with prompts to raise a change order
problem: Scope expands through chat messages and emails that start with a quick question, and by the time the project manager notices the work is under way.
approach: An agent compares client requests with agreed scope: in-scope ones pass, out-of-scope ones alert the project manager, and ambiguous ones are escalated.
A vendor guide describes this; Certinia's PMO Quality agent scans project scope regularly, and Oracle mentions AI-driven change management.
Vendor illustration, not a measurement: a USD 120,000 project scoped at 400 hours ran to 520, giving back USD 36,000 of margin.
The project manager makes the final call on each flagged request; the engagement lead decides whether to raise scope with the client.

title: Engagement margin and budget monitoring with alerts on overruns and missing timesheets
problem: Margin leaks during delivery but leadership sees it only in a report after month-end, which Teamwork calls the erosion gap.
approach: Agents watch actuals against plan and flag exceptions early; Rocketlane describes agents hunting for missing timesheets, un-invoiced hours and budget overruns.
Certinia, Kantata and Deltek describe similar monitoring; for law firms, BigHand Matter Pricing is marketed with automated overrun alerts.
Deltek states a 20% improvement in forecast accuracy from connecting people, projects and financials; the claim is about integration, not AI (vendor-published).
The project or finance lead acts on each alert; invoicing decisions stay with people.

title: Agent project manager keeps plans current and chases tasks as milestones move
problem: Plans go stale when milestones slip, and a project manager must reconcile task, calendar and time data by hand.
approach: Certinia lists a Project Manager Agent; Kantata says plans update automatically when milestones shift.
Rocketlane says agents do the heavy work while the team approves and intervenes when needed; Planview announced project-manager agents for Fall 2026.
Certinia claims up to 20 hours a month saved per project manager (vendor-published); no basis given.
Certinia also claims about 50% of project time historically lost to admin is recovered (vendor-published).

title: Idea: automated stakeholder reminders, calendar coordination and project-tool setup
problem: Idea, not a deployment: project managers lose time chasing stakeholders for time sheets, agendas and deadlines, scheduling across time zones and configuring project tools.
approach: Idea: in a study of 12 Finnish IT project-management consultants, calendar and meeting management was the most anticipated capability (four of 12).
Interviewees also wanted automated reminders to steering groups and partners, and automated tool configuration such as Jira setup (independent).
Human control of assistant tasks is the only checkpoint the sources specify.

title: Idea: predictive monitoring of dependencies, deviations and risks from project history
problem: Idea, not a deployment: external project managers find dependency management and early-warning signals hard to keep up by hand, and progress is analysed only when someone compiles the data.
approach: Idea: interviewees envisioned an assistant that watches data against baselines, flags dependencies that cannot be met and drafts risk assessments.
One interviewee tested Gemini on a migration-project framework and found it identified typical risks, but did not put it into practice.
The project manager reviews alerts and recommended actions.

title: Reusable matter templates route tasks to agents and people with review gates
problem: For recurring work such as an M&A transaction, the process is rebuilt for each matter and partners ask associates to reconstruct status from email.
approach: Harvey announced Legal Work Orchestration on 2026-10-15: a template pre-loads phases, tasks, agents and review gates, and each task carries a reviewer.
When an agent finishes a task, the designated partner is notified and approval starts the next step.
Tasks, comments and notifications are rolling out; templates are in early access; no measured results.
Harvey expects agents to take on an additional 20% of workflow steps within six months (vendor-published expectation).

title: Self-built PMO agent estate with an orchestrating agent and human approval gate
problem: Portfolio reporting is one of the last manual processes in many delivery organisations: assembled by hand, often late and open to challenge.
approach: Automation Consultants built a 12-agent estate across Jira, Confluence, Loom and Tempo, with Rovo at the centre and Claude as reasoning layer.
An orchestrating agent screens every finding, and a human approval gate sits before anything reaches Jira, Confluence or a client inbox.
The firm reports roughly 25% of delivery capacity released and throughput tripled across 11 concurrent client engagements (self-reported).
Vendors Productive and Kantata (Agent Studio, launched 2026-10-07) sell agent builders with approval or validation checks before output goes out.

title: Agents take on repeatable implementation tasks and send routine project documentation
problem: Implementation teams are asked to deliver more go-lives with the same headcount, and billable utilization is at a record low in SPI's benchmark.
approach: Basware's in-house services team adopted Kantata, automated billing first, and is expanding into agents that help staff projects.
AI is embedded to take on repetitive implementation work and to generate and send project documentation to customers.
Rocketlane is described by a competitor as claiming up to 50% lower delivery effort in early deployments (vendor-published).
A human gate and audit trail for agent actions touching customer environments is one vendor's evaluation criterion; people handle customer-specific tasks.

title: Engagement leads run advisory work as teams of people and AI agents
problem: Delivery planning assumes work is divided among people; a firm using AI for analysis, modelling and documentation must decide what goes to agents and who checks it.
approach: Thoughtworks' Engagement Lead and Principal Engagement Lead postings call them delivery leaders for AI-native advisory engagements.
They structure each engagement across team members, AI agents and client stakeholders, and delegate to AI while keeping quality and judgment.
They capture reusable delivery patterns and AI workflows in a shared library; the postings describe expectations, not results (self-reported).
The engagement lead is accountable for output accuracy, relevance and readiness for decision.

title: Idea: engagement economics that count AI cost, effort and fee basis
problem: Idea, not a deployment: when agents do part of delivery, utilization and time-and-materials metrics no longer show who did the work or what it cost.
approach: Idea: meter AI use per matter so its cost is attributable to the client, budgeted and possibly passed through.
Idea: during delivery, compare actual effort, AI-assisted effort and fee basis, flagging fixed-fee work where effort has fallen well below the fee.
Planview's agent launch covers costing agents and compute spend; a Kantata and Basware session on agent margin was scheduled for 2026-10-20.
Pricing and finance leaders decide what AI cost passes through; one law firm officer cited roughly 1% of revenue (self-reported).
